description: Use for head-to-head 'X vs Y' questions about crypto and company taxes — e.g. 'crypto taxes Germany vs Czechia', 'is Dubai or Singapore better for corporate tax', 'Portugal vs Spain for a crypto investor'. Give two countries `country1` and `country2` (ISO-3166 code or English name). Returns side-by-side headline rates with the source's wording per rate in `rates_detail`, treaty counts, crypto tier, and the tax-only scoring dimension (`tax_score`, with `zero_tax_rate` saying whether a 0% estimate is `firm` or `conditional`). A comparison answers `depends_on_conditions` instead of naming a winner when either rate is a range or conditional. The income and capital-gains figures describe how CRYPTO is taxed and `corporate` is the headline company rate; salary income tax brackets are not covered (see `coverage_note`). Each country also carries `general_rates`: the OECD's combined statutory company income tax rate and top personal income tax rate with year and citation, null where the OECD does not cover the country or the figure is held back (then listed under `withheld` with the reason). Company tax is compared twice and the answers can differ: `comparison.lower_corporate_tax` uses the crypto source's `corporate` figure (sometimes the central-government rate alone, sometimes simply older), `comparison.lower_corporate_tax_oecd` uses the OECD's combined rate; for a general company tax question use the OECD one. `tax_found: false` means no crypto-tax rows for that country; its `general_rates` can still be filled. A null treaty_count means no data on file. To rank more than two countries use compare_jurisdictions.

country1.description: First country: ISO-3166 alpha-2/alpha-3 code or English name, e.g. 'PT' or 'Portugal'.

country2.description: Second country: ISO-3166 alpha-2/alpha-3 code or English name, e.g. 'ES' or 'Spain'.

name: tax_compare
title: Compare taxes between two countries
